_note: The Exploration tree — the exploration age, 1200 → 1660 CE (TREES.md § The store; ../EXPLORATION.md owns the phase). Invested: the Invest verb takes one node a round, chosen by the scorer.

A MOCK-UP (Ben, 2026-09-11, resolving NR-843). The shape, the branches, the three forks and the milestone chain are the design; every per_mille is a placeholder the sweep re-prices, exactly as the other three trees' are.
EXPLORATION_TREE.md is the authority; this file transcribes its tables. tree_lint.js cross-checks the two both ways and enforces the five rules.

Ids carry branch and ring (EX-
-; seq m is the ring's milestone). Links are undirected, declared on the node farther from the root; the root EX-SP-1a lists none, and that empty list is how the generated table derives is_root (tree_lint holds exactly one).
Names are generic mechanism nouns — real history is a mechanism reference, never a name source; earth_ref is calibration prose only.

branches.name: The Purse (the spire)
branches.concern: material becomes capital, and capital acquires an institution that outlives a reign — the phase's clock

branches.name: Hulls
branches.concern: what can cross, how much it carries, and whether it arrives able to fight

branches.name: Port & Garrison
branches.concern: the harbour that stages a crossing, and the standing force a neighbour can see

branches.name: Ways
branches.concern: the road ladder's third rung and the throughput that runs on it

branches.name: Goods
branches.concern: what a people does with a good it did not grow — naming it, counting it, wanting it

nodes.name: Consolidated Stores

effects.target: the treasury stands at the capital

pursued_when.situation: Seats hold materials the realm cannot spend as one; gathering them to the capital is the cheapest increase in what can be bought.

nodes.earth_ref: the fisc centralises; a realm stops being a set of provisioned cities

nodes.name: The Common Purse

pursued_when.situation: A realm with a harbour and a posted road can gather what its seats hold into one purse, and spend it where it chooses. Ring 2 opens.

nodes.earth_ref: a single treasury, reachable and defensible

nodes.name: The Chartered Company

effects.target: an entity that outlives its members may hold capital and bind a term

pursued_when.situation: The purse cannot fund a distant venture from one reign's revenue; an entity that persists can borrow against the next.

nodes.earth_ref: the joint venture with a life of its own

nodes.name: The Standing Charter

pursued_when.situation: A market to trade in, a force to be seen holding, and hulls of one kind or the other. A promise can now run for years. Ring 3 opens.

nodes.earth_ref: contract with a term, enforced at a distance

nodes.name: Double-Entry Reckoning

pursued_when.situation: Nothing binds; the realm buys the ability to know what it is owed, which compounds into everything else.

nodes.earth_ref: accounts that survive the accountant

nodes.name: The Long Reckoning

pursued_when.situation: A realm that knows what a good is worth to whom, can reach it, and can carry it. The rim: the Industry tree opens when digitisation does.

nodes.earth_ref: capital, accounted and mobile — the threshold of an industrial economy

nodes.name: Decked Coaster

effects.target: a crossing may be staged from a held port

pursued_when.situation: The realm holds water frontage and wants what is across it; a decked hull is the first thing that survives the passage.

nodes.earth_ref: the coaster that dares the open leg

nodes.name: Sounding & Chart

pursued_when.situation: Taken on the way to a larger hull; a known depth is a passage that can be repeated.

nodes.earth_ref: the lead line and the written coast

nodes.name: Careening & Refit

pursued_when.situation: A hull that can be kept is a hull that stays at sea; the shared step before the realm chooses what kind of fleet it wants.

nodes.earth_ref: the careening beach; a hull maintained rather than replaced

nodes.name: Ocean Carrack

pursued_when.situation: The realm wants goods it cannot grow and knows where they are; burden, not broadside, is what closes that gap.

nodes.earth_ref: the bulk carrier: cargo first, guns as an afterthought

nodes.name: Fleet of the Line

pursued_when.situation: A neighbour's hulls are visible and the realm would rather contest the water than carry across it.

nodes.earth_ref: the fighting fleet; a navy that denies rather than delivers

nodes.name: Oceanic Navigation

effects.target: a crossing to unmet ground no longer requires an adjacent shore

pursued_when.situation: Every want the realm can reach is already met; the remaining ones are across water nobody has crossed.

nodes.earth_ref: latitude, then longitude — a passage that can be repeated blind

nodes.name: Harbour Works

pursued_when.situation: The realm holds ground with a port window and nothing built on it; the harbour is what turns endowment into a staging place.

nodes.earth_ref: mole, quay and a dredged approach

nodes.name: Pilot & Lighthouse

pursued_when.situation: A harbour a stranger's hull can enter at night is a harbour that earns; taken alongside the works.

nodes.earth_ref: the marked approach

nodes.name: Standing Garrison

effects.target: force already raised; visible to neighbours

pursued_when.situation: Neighbours can see what the realm keeps standing, and a force already raised is what makes a treaty cheaper than a test.

nodes.earth_ref: the permanent establishment; deterrence as a running cost

nodes.name: Naval Stores

pursued_when.situation: Cordage, pitch and timber kept at the quay; the difference between a fleet that sails and one that is listed.

nodes.earth_ref: the victualling yard

nodes.name: Dry Dock

pursued_when.situation: The shared step before the realm decides whether its coast projects force or refuses it.

nodes.earth_ref: the graving dock; hulls repaired rather than abandoned

nodes.name: Blue-Water Squadron

effects.target: force projected to ground the realm does not hold

pursued_when.situation: The realm holds something across water and must be able to reach it faster than a rival can take it.

nodes.earth_ref: the standing squadron on a distant station

nodes.name: Fortified Roadstead

pursued_when.situation: The realm would rather no hull entered its water at all than own hulls that leave it.

nodes.earth_ref: chain, battery and a defended anchorage

nodes.name: Post Roads

effects.target: Road becomes Highway on a corridor that carries

pursued_when.situation: The realm's own ground is the constraint: corridors that carry are worn past what a Road answers, and the next rung is the cheapest relief.

nodes.earth_ref: the maintained trunk line; the third rung above track and road

nodes.name: Bonded Warehouse

effects.target: goods may stand in transit without a holder

pursued_when.situation: The corridor carries more than the far end can absorb; a place to hold goods mid-route is what stops throughput capping at the destination.

nodes.earth_ref: the entrepôt; goods at rest but not at home

nodes.name: Wayhouse Relay

pursued_when.situation: The shared step before the realm chooses whether its bulk moves overland or on water.

nodes.earth_ref: staged relays; a load handed on rather than hauled through

nodes.name: Trunk Highway

pursued_when.situation: The realm is continental and its constraint is interior distance; the road answers both trade and the march.

nodes.earth_ref: the all-weather trunk; distance collapsed by surface

nodes.name: Canal Cut

pursued_when.situation: Bulk is the constraint rather than speed; water carriage moves tonnage a road never will, and only on ground that permits the cut.

nodes.earth_ref: inland water carriage; bulk over pace

nodes.name: Toll & Escort

pursued_when.situation: A route that pays for its own protection; the point at which the ways branch and the garrison branch stop being separate concerns.

nodes.earth_ref: the escorted convoy, paid for by what it carries

nodes.name: Named Staples

effects.target: goods are named and countable rather than an undifferentiated store

pursued_when.situation: The realm lacks something and cannot say what; naming the staples is what turns a shortage into a want with a direction.

nodes.earth_ref: the staple: a good with a name, a measure and a place it is sold

nodes.name: Weights & Tally

pursued_when.situation: A measure two parties agree on; the smallest thing that makes a good countable at both ends of a road.

nodes.earth_ref: the standard measure, enforced

nodes.name: Quayside Market

effects.target: a market's scarcity signal is legible to a stranger

pursued_when.situation: The realm's own market must be readable before a stranger will sail to it; legibility is what converts a want into an arrival.

nodes.earth_ref: the open quay where a price is asked aloud

nodes.name: Bill of Lading

pursued_when.situation: A claim on goods that are somewhere else; what lets a cargo be owned while it is still moving.

nodes.earth_ref: the transferable claim on a shipment

nodes.name: Standing Preference

effects.target: a people's preference for a good is durable and readable across the contact graph

pursued_when.situation: Nothing binds materially; the realm buys knowledge of what other peoples will keep paying for, which is what a trading age compounds on.

nodes.earth_ref: taste becomes a market fact rather than a curiosity

nodes.name: Factor's Ledger

pursued_when.situation: An agent kept at a foreign market, reporting what it holds and wants; the cheapest intelligence a trading realm buys.

nodes.earth_ref: the resident factor, writing home
